text:
maria: Heads-up: after last runtime rollout p50 token latency for seq8k increased ~7% on prod serving group 'stream-100'. Saw it at ~11:14 UTC. Symptoms look like a big drop in KV cache hit-rate during warm bursts.

kevin: Can you paste the trace/span IDs? I'll grab flame graphs.

maria: trace=span_0x9f3a7b... logs show repeated 'cache_miss: key_mismatch' lines. Also noticed kernel selection picked 'matmul-v2' for a subset of models in the same window.

profiler-bot: ```prefix-cache: hit_rate=0.72 -> 0.58 (post-deploy)
avg_token_latency=11.2ms -> 12.0ms (+6.8%)
eviction_rate=1.0/s -> 3.2/s
GPU_mem_free=320MB -> 48MB```

john: Did we change key normalization recently? There was a PR that switched to sha256(salt+prompt) to avoid collisions: <https://github.com/redwood/pr/1234|pr/1234>.

sara: We did that in the compile path for kernel selection only, supposed to be a no-op for runtime keys, but maybe the salt isn't shared between compile/prefill/runtime.

maria: Reproduced locally with loadgen: confirmed a miss-storm during warmup. Hit-rate drops from ~80% to ~40% in first 30s. If I disable CPU prefill the spike doesn't appear.

kevin: pprof + diff suggest the runtime v1.2.3 binary uses new salt; prefill workers are still on v1.2.1. Keys differ -> effectively duplicate keys stored, causing fragmentation and faster evictions on hot shards. Patch idea: unify key derivation or add explicit key-version header so mismatches surface.

sara: Short-term mitigation proposal: TTL for prefix keys 60s -> 300s and bump per-shard cache target size +20% to reduce churn. Concern: memory bump.

john: Charts show slab fragmentation spikes when duplicates appear; increasing TTL reduces churn but duplicates still waste slots. We should avoid wasting entries rather than just letting them live longer.

kevin: Ran an A/B: TTL=300 + shard+20% -> hit-rate 0.67 -> 0.74, p50 latency returned to baseline. Memory used +12% but no OOM in 24h canary. Eviction reasons: previously 70% fragmentation, now 15% fragmentation and majority age-based evictions.

maria: Good signal. Long-term actions: 1) enforce keying-consistency across prefill/runtime/compile, 2) add key-salt-version header to cache entries for debug, 3) evaluate age-weighted LRU or segmented-LRU to prefer compactness and reduce fragmentation.

sara: I'll schedule rolling prefill workers to v1.2.3 in staging tonight. Will also open a dashboard tile for key-salt-mismatch and eviction-reason breakdown.

john: Follow-ups created: KEV-112 (key-version header + validation), KEV-113 (seg-LRU perf bench), KEV-114 (kernel-selection should not mutate key derivation). I'll own KEV-113.

maria: Thanks all. We'll keep the TTL bump as a temporary guard until KEV-112 is done. @ops please mute the fragmentation pager and add a lower-severity alert for key-salt-mismatch. :thumbsup:
